properties.note: Traced on the USGS Flushing 1:24,000 sheet, 1966 edition (scan 137330): the dashed strip from 20th Avenue south-south-east along Linden Place, 877 m (2,880 ft) x 30 m — the '2,950 ft paved runway' of the 1962 AOPA directory. Paving year ESTIMATED 1957: 'an unpaved landing area' on c. 1951 and 1954 air photos, '2 paved runways' on the July 1960 sectional chart (Abandoned & Little-Known Airfields). The same dry strip crosses the marsh on the 1947 sheet. Ends with the airport, 1984 (the asphalt lay derelict and flooded afterwards).

Traced on the same sheet: the dashed strip from 20th Avenue south-west to the foot of the north-south runway, 797 m (2,615 ft) x 28 m. Paved by July 1960 ('2 paved runways'); 'NE/SW runway closed' on the 1965 sectional chart but still drawn on the 1966 sheet: kept to 1984 (ESTIMATED).

Grass landing strip (Miller Field 'had a grass runway ... the last airport with a grass runway in New York City', Wikipedia) as drawn dashed on the USGS The Narrows 1:24,000 sheet of 1955 (scan 139985): 975 m x 44 m from the Hylan Boulevard corner east-south-east. NOT pavement: not drawn by airports.py.
Second grass strip on the same sheet, 601 m x 36 m, from Elm Tree Avenue toward the hangars at the shore. NOT pavement.
